patch.value: Derived scheduling: propagate milestone deadlines backward through the ordering graph so every gating item carries a latest-start date instead of only six dates existing in the whole plan

Latest-start dates are derived for every item on an ordering path to a dated item, from that item's deadline and the estimates on the path, and are reported as derived rather than stored as authored deadlines; Slack is reported in time units alongside the existing topological layer slack, so an item with layer slack and no date slack is distinguishable from one with both; A path whose accumulated estimates cannot fit between now and the gated deadline is reported as an over-committed path, naming the deadline, the path and the shortfall; Items with no estimate are reported as an explicit unschedulable residual rather than being treated as zero-duration, so the derivation never silently manufactures feasibility; Derivation is bounded and stays inside the graph analytics token and latency budgets at million-item scale, and degrades to a declared partial result rather than a full scan; A negative control proves the over-commitment finding fires when a deadline is moved earlier than its path allows and clears when it is moved back
Any dated commitment implies a dated constraint on every item that gates it, computed from the recorded graph rather than asserted item by item

A plan whose only dates sit on its endpoints cannot be late until it already is. Six dates across 339 open items means no item can ever report as at-risk, and the earliest possible warning is the milestone date itself.
Turns the six outcome milestones from declared intent into a schedule the record can check, and gives every relevance and next-work signal a real urgency input instead of a priority integer.

Latest-start and slack are reported in dates for every item on a path to a dated commitment, derived and reproducible, and a path whose estimates no longer fit its deadline is a finding rather than a surprise.

The milestone ladder now carries deadlines from 2026-10-31 to 2028-06-30 and a coherent blocker DAG, so the inputs for derivation exist for the first time; the analytic that would consume them computes in layers and ignores dates.

patch.value:
## The census

Open items (open, in_progress, blocked, draft): 339. Carrying a deadline: 6. Those six are exactly the outcome milestones. Every other open item is undated.

The nineteen items that directly gate the six milestones by `blocked_by` — pm-pbyu, pm-1kxs, pm-usfg, pm-xpumg4, pm-9yfo, pm-9rxu, pm-2sbj8p, pm-atfm, pm-tch9cs, pm-4k6b, pm-agou, pm-zclzll, pm-rtn5h6, pm-pae3wo, pm-ygli86, pm-8jdc, pm-li2fj5, pm-nfrhf0, pm-t8a0x1 — carry no deadline between them.

## The plan that exists and is coherent

The milestone layer is genuinely well formed, which is why derivation is now possible:

| milestone | deadline | est. min | gated by |
|---|---|---|---|
| pm-j82fd3 command grammar | 2026-10-31 | 4,800 | pbyu, 1kxs |
| pm-9rgaal SDK-complete core | 2026-12-31 | 6,000 | j82fd3, usfg, xpumg4 |
| pm-w7ccmv provable history | 2027-03-31 | 5,400 | 9yfo |
| pm-o87av6 proven scale | 2027-09-30 | 9,600 | 9rgaal, 9rxu, 2sbj8p, atfm, tch9cs, 4k6b |
| pm-xp1xsw v1.0 GA contract | 2027-12-31 | 3,600 | 9rgaal, agou, j82fd3, w7ccmv, o87av6, zclzll, rtn5h6, pae3wo, ygli86 |
| pm-t4d7nz universal platform | 2028-06-30 | 12,000 | 9rgaal, w7ccmv, o87av6, xp1xsw, 8jdc, li2fj5, nfrhf0, t8a0x1 |

Every milestone's deadline is later than every milestone that gates it, so the dated layer is internally consistent. The ordering is a genuine DAG, not a ring. The estimates are present. All three inputs a backward pass needs are already recorded.

## Why the existing analytic cannot answer it

`pm graph slack` on this tracker reports `makespan: 10`, `scheduled_count: 560`, `critical_count: 22`, `critical_path_length: 9`. Those are topological layers. The unit is hops, not time. So the surface that computes slack cannot read the six deadlines, and the six deadlines constrain nothing the surface computes.

The consequence is that "critical" currently means "on the longest chain of hops", which is not the same as "on the path that will miss its date". An item can sit on a nine-hop critical path with two years of date slack, and an item one hop from a milestone can be the only thing that will actually be late. Today those rank identically.

## Boundary, so this does not become date fabrication

The derivation must produce *derived latest-start*, never an authored `deadline`. Writing dates onto 333 items would create a second schedule to disagree with the first, and would make the numbers unfalsifiable — exactly the failure mode a hand-maintained ledger always produces. The dates stay computed, the inputs stay the recorded deadline plus the recorded estimates plus the recorded edges, and an item with no estimate is reported as unschedulable rather than assumed instantaneous.

That residual is large today and should be visible from the first run: estimates exist widely, but the 915 items missing `estimated_minutes` across all statuses are exactly the population that would otherwise be silently treated as free.
